definitions.explanation: The number six when counting things using native Japanese numbers.

examples.japanese: {六|むっ}つ{残|のこ}っています。
たまごを{六|むっ}つ{買|か}いました。
お{皿|さら}を{六|むっ}つ{出|だ}してください。{今日|きょう}は{六人|ろくにん}です。
examples.english: Please take out six plates. We have six people today.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{六|むっ}つの{時|とき}に{小学校|しょうがっこう}に{入|はい}ります。
examples.english: Children enter elementary school when they are six.

notes:
{六|むっ}つ is the native Japanese number for counting six general items.

NATIVE COUNTING SYSTEM (1-10):
- {一|ひと}つ (1), {二|ふた}つ (2), {三|みっ}つ (3), {四|よっ}つ (4), {五|いつ}つ (5)
- {六|むっ}つ (6), {七|なな}つ (7), {八|やっ}つ (8), {九|ここの}つ (9), {十|とお} (10)

WHEN TO USE:
- General objects without specific counters
- Age up to 9: {六|むっ}つ = 6 years old
- Abstract things: {理由|りゆう}が{六|むっ}つ (six reasons)

CHINESE VS. NATIVE:
- {六|ろく}: Sino-Japanese (used with counters like {個|こ}, {本|ほん})
- {六|むっ}つ: Native Japanese (standalone counting)

EXAMPLE CONTRAST:
- りんごを{六|むっ}つ: six apples (native)
- りんごを{六|ろっ}{個|こ}: six apples (Sino-Japanese + counter)
